title: Install and maintain Platter
summary: Install Platter through its declared setup command, or perform explicit maintenance and migration while preserving packet and delivery history.
use_when: The user wants Platter installed, replaced, inspected or maintained.
The caller needs prerequisite readiness, admission holds, draining or supported installed-release verification.
An operator must preserve a separately managed Clockwork daily binding while upgrading its pinned Platter runner.
do_not_use_when: The requested outcome is packet preparation, a test email, opportunity discovery, profile editing or scheduled delivery.
The caller expects arbitrary direct rollback, a schema reset or implicit installation of dependencies.
outcome: An installation with matching Platter command and provider, supported maintenance state, or a local readiness result. Stored domain history remains intact.

interfaces.label: Print the selected release daily failure policy without activation

effects: The declared product command selects program and provider files through owned selectors. It starts no packet preparation or email.
Durable owner holds fence new mutations while exact admitted work drains. Explicit migration preserves retained identities and removes only hashed legacy files after transactional import.

Separately requested read-only checks inspect installation, state and dependency readiness without domain work. Explicit supplied setup can initialize missing templates or activation intent. The product command retargets existing schedules directly and preserves saved or explicit enabled intent and incidents.

The product deployment command selects program and provider files, then migrates or initializes state, imports explicitly supplied templates, updates executable references and selects its owned daily definition under ordinary admission and activity locks. It invokes no doctor, creates no hold, does not drain durable requester work. It disables its enabled Clockwork bindings and waits for their current activations before runtime publication. Runtime diagnostics and explicit maintenance remain separate.

Program publication copies the selected release into fixed regular files beneath ~/Library/Application Support/Platter/install/runtime. Public commands use that runtime tree; current and previous retain immutable UUID archive selections. Code signing and runtime path identity are separate from release identity. New Clockwork definitions use schema 3: they retain the archive release ID, root and exact hashes, and execute the fixed runtime image. Publication precedes registration. Before publication, deployment runs the disable transition for owned Clockwork bindings and waits for their active processes, including an active manual run on a disabled binding. It restores saved enabled intent after registration; a failed instruction can leave the owned bindings disabled. Existing history, delivery records, enabled intent and incident halts retain their meaning. Retained definitions and wrapper bytes from before this change keep their legacy execution paths until a new installation or definition selects the runtime image.
authority: Platter owns domain compatibility, admission, drain policy, retained state and success. Nucleus owns execution state and cancellation.

Telete executes explicit selected product instructions; the shared file helper owns release metadata, selector ownership, writer locks and individual atomic replacements. It performs no automatic selector compensation.
Catalog presence, a successful build or stored delivery time grants no installation, send, recurring-delivery or dependency-upgrade authority.
success: Declared resource placement and product setup commands complete. Saved or explicit schedule intent and failure incidents remain preserved; application readiness and explicit maintenance completion need their separate evidence.
failure_and_recovery: A failed instruction retains completed file, migration, configuration and schedule changes. The executor stops and performs no automatic retry, rollback or product recovery. Interrupted commands have unknown effects. Inspect current product state and complete authorized recovery separately from executor reconciliation and acknowledgement. Preserve separately acquired holds.

Use explicit product interfaces to inspect retained effects and complete authorized recovery. An interrupted executor request executes no automatic repair; a new attempt requires a new request ID. Preserve separately acquired maintenance holds and migration evidence.
Schema-eight state cannot use an older incompatible binary. Program selection does not undo migration; select a compatible program for explicit recovery.
Preserve Clockwork halts and uncertain sends through deployment. Binding continuation does not authorize a preparation retry or ambiguous resend.
privacy: Private state contains career history, original resume and packet/send metadata. It remains separate from immutable public installation material and source control.

Installation manifests retain executable/provider identity and local paths, never private resume bodies or provider keys. Model and email disclosures belong only to separately authorized runtime operations.
does_not_authorize: Preparing packets, sending email or submitting replacement Nucleus work.
Installing or enabling a daily schedule, changing provider credentials/billing or upgrading unselected dependencies.
Resetting sent flags, deleting retained artifacts, changing fixed resume content or bypassing an unresolved maintenance hold.

consumers.statement: The current user and Cell coordinator use the supported inspection, readiness, maintenance, migration, and installation procedures.

preconditions.statement: Use exact committed source, explicit selected products and owned artifact paths. Product setup uses ordinary admission and activity locks; an existing hold can refuse it. The executor adds no dependencies or maintenance requesters. Explicit maintenance and migration retain their sole-owner and drain prerequisites.

inputs.statement: Submit ./ci.sh submit COMMIT --deploy platter from the Cell root. CI and Telete are the sole deployment route. --settings ABSOLUTE_JSON supplies private JSON whose platter object contains explicit resume, projects_template or enabled choices. Telete freezes settings and retains exact source, request and artifact correlation. Explicit migration can request a private product completion receipt. Use the fixed Vita selection and complete Bazaar prompt prerequisites defined by required runtime features.

outputs.statement: Selected owned program, installer and provider files, generic execution outcomes and product-owned migration or setup effects. Explicit diagnostics and maintenance supply their own observations.

data_semantics.statement: Use platter.maintenance for release, canonical schema-eight state, hold/drain, migration, and incident meaning. Platter state and Nucleus evidence/credentials remain separately owned.

identity_and_units.statement: Source commit and executor request ID correlate delivery. Exact owner IDs identify separately acquired maintenance holds. Preserve packet, request, edition and send identities without treating owner identity as process liveness.

operational_limits.statement: Installation prepares no packets and sends no email. Missing-template initialization and first-time activation require explicit supplied setup. Explicit cancellation excludes unrelated Weaver jobs.
No installation latency, arbitrary incompatible rollback, future support interval or deprecation window is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: CI and Telete are the sole deployment route. The product deploy command, explicit maintenance interfaces, retained execution receipts, and transactional migration and hashed source-cleanup rules remain supported.

Schemas two through seven migrate owned discovery opportunity and configuration names to Milieu without changing captured requests, artifacts, editions, eligibility or opaque identities. Older programs cannot open schema eight.

reliances.statement: Nucleus supplies compatible execution health and cancellation of matching orphaned jobs.
Runtime prerequisites rely on Milieu retained export, Annals commands and Email attachment support; unselected installations are not upgraded implicitly.

Telete validates, prepares signed programs and executes explicitly selected ordered product instructions. It retains source and request correlation and process outcomes. Products own setup, state, maintenance and recovery.
Resume readiness depends on Tectonic, Python 3 with pypdf, and the original template packages/fonts.

The product-owned schema-three definition declares halt-until-approved. Clockwork owns activation, the shared service-health delay before a new durable halt, incident email and exact continuation approval; Platter owns expected readiness outcomes, date selection and preserved preparation/delivery recovery.
Weaver authors private project Markdown through its typed installed CLI client, with caller-supplied identity and exact-request recovery. It owns its Annals reads and Nucleus jobs.

Bazaar owns immutable text versions, shared selection format and loading, template rendering, and trusted reference expansion. The caller owns authored meaning, component policy, runtime inputs, request assembly, permissions, execution policy, and domain success; prompt text grants no additional authority.

session_surfaces: Cell checkout and installed Telete manager
owned Platter release and canonical private state
steps: Select the exact committed source, explicit product set and authorized setup settings; preserve canonical private state.
Preview the declared product instructions and select required dependency updates explicitly.
Run the manifest product command to place resources and perform migration, initialization, configuration or explicitly supplied imports under ordinary admission.
Preserve saved or explicit schedule intent and failure incidents while selecting the updated product definition.
Read retained instruction outcomes. Use doctor or owner-scoped maintenance separately when their effects and observations are intended.
Inspect failed or interrupted effects through product interfaces. Complete authorized recovery separately from executor reconciliation and acknowledgement.
checkpoints: The caller explicitly selects the complete authorized product set; the executor adds no dependency or maintenance scope.
Source and request correlation and owned selector boundaries remain exact.
Migration preserves retained domain identities and its transactional import and hashed source-cleanup rules.
Deployment completion means declared commands and placements completed; no health, readiness or automatic recovery claim follows.
adaptation: Use read-only inspection or state-only diagnosis separately from deployment and domain work.
Use explicit owner-scoped maintenance and drain only when that operation is authorized; manifest deployment creates and releases no hold.
Retain completed effects after failure. A new executor attempt needs a new request ID and does not imply retry of uncertain mail or model work.
stop_when: A declared instruction fails, ordinary admission is held, a file input cannot be placed, or a selector is foreign.
Migration source or receipt evidence conflicts, state is unsupported, or a binary-only rollback would cross incompatible state.
Recovery would reset domain history, resend uncertain mail, release a foreign hold, upgrade an unselected dependency or clear a Clockwork halt.
